name: Guided by Voices
label: Matador
lede: A Dayton fourth-grade teacher who once pitched a college no-hitter made records on a four-track for a decade nobody heard, quit, got discovered, and has now put out forty-four albums under one band name.

eras.title: A teacher's band nobody outside Dayton heard
eras.text: Robert Pollard, a former Wright State pitcher teaching fourth grade in Dayton, Ohio, led a bar band that became a basement recording project. For nearly a decade Guided by Voices paid to press records in runs of a few hundred that almost nobody bought.

years.src: Wikipedia: Robert Pollard · Wikipedia: Guided by Voices
years.h: [[Robert Pollard|e7f29e49-6078-4528-a5dc-5d0eeb8a1437]] starts Guided by Voices as a Dayton bar band
years.p: Robert Pollard pitched a no-hitter for Wright State but quit sports and became a schoolteacher, settling on fourth grade. The band starts with his brother Jim Pollard, Mitch Mitchell and Kevin Fennell.
years.xp:
Pollard picked teaching partly for the vacation time, which he spent on music. He taught for about 14 years, and school life turned up in songs like Gold Star for Robot Boy and Teenage FBI.

Pollard has since registered nearly 3,000 songs with BMI.

years.h: [[Tobin Sprout|4b05ba8c-0f7b-4735-b8c1-153a5875a4d8]] joins, bringing songs and a home studio
years.p: Tobin Sprout, an Ohio University-trained illustrator, joins Guided by Voices as second songwriter, guitarist and engineer.

years.h: Devil Between My Toes and Sandbox, a few hundred copies each
years.p: Guided by Voices self-finances its early albums after the EP Forever Since Breakfast, pressing only a few hundred of each. Self-Inflicted Aerial Nostalgia and Same Place the Fly Got Smashed follow.

years.src: Wikipedia: Propeller · Wikipedia: Guided by Voices
years.h: Propeller: a goodbye album in 500 handmade sleeves
years.p: Deep in debt, Robert Pollard meant Propeller as the band's last record. Each of the 500 vinyl sleeves was hand-decorated with paint, screen prints and found objects.
years.xp:
The opening crowd chant of G-B-V was faked in the studio: the band had barely played live. Fans have chanted it at shows ever since. By 2005, original sleeves reportedly sold for thousands of dollars.

College radio, and praise from [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] and [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]], got the record heard outside Dayton.

years.h: Robert Pollard breaks up the band and teaches full-time
years.p: After Propeller, Robert Pollard ends Guided by Voices and commits to teaching full-time. By 1993 the band was back.

eras.title: Four-tracks, beer and the classic five
eras.text: The line-up of Pollard, Sprout, Mitchell, Greg Demos and Kevin Fennell played outside Ohio for the first time, and Bee Thousand made them an indie-rock cause. Matador signed them, and Pollard quit teaching.

years.h: Vampire on Titus, named for Pollard's Dayton street
years.p: Made by just Robert Pollard, Jim Pollard and Tobin Sprout, it's often called the harshest lo-fi record in the catalog. The title comes from a line about sucking songs out of the earth on Titus Avenue.
years.xp: Jim Shepard of V-3 once told Pollard he pulled songs out of the ground like a vampire on Titus, the Dayton avenue where Pollard lived. Scat released it, with Propeller appended.

years.h: The classic five play New York and Philadelphia
years.p: With Robert Pollard, Tobin Sprout, Mitch Mitchell, Greg Demos and Kevin Fennell, Guided by Voices plays outside Ohio for the first time.

years.h: Bee Thousand: a nearly-final album becomes a landmark
years.p: Built mostly from old songs on Portastudios in Dayton garages and basements, with mistakes left in. Pitchfork later ranked it No. 10 of the 1990s.
years.xp:
Pollard was thinking about ending the band for money reasons. His rule: if nobody was listening anyway, he'd put exactly what he wanted on the record. Most songs took about 30 minutes with no rehearsal; the guitar drops out on Hardcore UFO's and Mincer Ray.

The cover comes from a National Geographic Mardi Gras story. The title mixes a mile marker, Z1000 or zoo thousand, with a misspelled Beethoven.

years.h: Robert Pollard leaves the classroom for good
years.p: After Bee Thousand, Pollard and his bandmates quit their day jobs to do music full-time, and major labels start calling.

q: if you leave out the beer, was about ten dollars
James Greer, on the recording cost
years.h: Alien Lanes: a big Matador advance, a tiny recording bill
years.p: Guided by Voices' first Matador album came with an advance of nearly $100,000, one of the label's biggest deals then. The band made 27 songs at Tobin Sprout's home studio anyway.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave it 9.2 and put it at No. 27 in its top 100 of the 1990s; Magnet named it album of 1995. Robert Christgau called it a dud.

James Greer, who played bass in the band in the mid-1990s, later wrote its history.

years.h: Motor Away is the single from Alien Lanes
years.p: Matador releases Motor Away as a single two months after Alien Lanes.

years.src: Wikipedia: Under the Bushes Under the Stars
years.h: Under the Bushes: 24 tracks, [[Kim Deal|760e4df4-e851-46c8-b34d-afa2e9706831]] and [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]
years.p: Guided by Voices moves to 24-track studios, with Kim Deal and Steve Albini among the producers, but Robert Pollard still sings through guitar amps. Matador asked for six extra songs at the end.
years.xp: Sessions ran through at least four studios and several producer teams. It was the last classic-line-up album until Let's Go Eat the Factory in 2012.

years.cap: Two solo records, one release day
years.src: Wikipedia: Guided by Voices · Wikipedia: Tobin Sprout
years.h: Tobin Sprout quits touring. He and Pollard release solo albums the same day
years.p: Tobin Sprout steps back to raise his child, paint and make solo records. His Carnival Boy and Robert Pollard's Not in My Airforce come out the same day, each man playing on the other's.
years.xp: Sprout went on to paint and publish children's books; Tim Allen has said he collects Sprout's artwork. Sprout and Pollard later worked together again as Airport 5 in 2001.

eras.title: Guided by Verde, then the big-label try
eras.text: Pollard kept the name and hired Cleveland's Cobra Verde, then built a harder-rocking band around Doug Gillard. A Ric Ocasek-produced album aimed at radio missed, the shows grew to three hours, and in 2004 Pollard called time.

years.h: Mag Earwhig!: Pollard fronts Cleveland's Cobra Verde
years.p: Robert Pollard keeps the name and uses Cobra Verde, with [[Doug Gillard|e1cfd005-e293-4196-af38-3a0ac0ab1dbe]], as his band. The classic line-up appears one last time on Jane of the Waking Universe. The Guided by Verde line-up splits late in 1997.

years.h: Do the Collapse: [[Ric Ocasek|697d4510-c3fe-4e96-bcc9-34739bccde8f]] polishes GBV, radio shrugs
years.p: Made for Capitol but released on TVT, the Ric Ocasek-produced album is slick and heavily processed. It gets mixed reviews and no radio breakthrough.

years.h: Guided by Voices shows stretch past three hours
years.p: The band plays marathon sets of new songs, classics, Robert Pollard solo tracks and covers of [[The Who|9fdaa16b-a6c4-4831-b87c-bc9ca8ce7eaa]], David Bowie and [[The Rolling Stones|b071f9fa-14b0-4217-8e97-eb41da73f598]], touring as far as Japan and New Zealand in 2000.

years.h: Suitcase: 100 unreleased songs in a four-disc box
years.p: Robert Pollard empties the vault: four discs, 100 songs spanning three decades.

years.h: Back to Matador with Universal Truths and Cycles
years.p: After leaving TVT, Guided by Voices returns to Matador and to its mid-1990s sound, with Todd Tobias producing.

q: This feels like the last album for Guided by Voices.
years.h: Robert Pollard ends Guided by Voices after Half Smiles
years.p: Robert Pollard says Half Smiles of the Decomposed is the final-album record he'd always said would end the band.

years.h: Last TV spot: Raincloud on Conan
years.p: Guided by Voices plays Everybody Thinks I'm a Raincloud (When I'm Not Looking) on Late Night with Conan O'Brien.

years.h: Four hours, 63 songs: the last show at Chicago's Metro
years.p: Guided by Voices ends on New Year's Eve with a 63-song marathon at the Metro in Chicago, released on DVD as The Electrifying Conclusion.

eras.title: The classic five come back
eras.text: Matador's 21st birthday brought back the 1993–96 line-up, and the reunion turned into six albums in three years. It ended with a fight over a drum kit and a Facebook post.

years.h: The classic line-up reunites for Matador at 21 in Las Vegas
years.p: Announced in June, the 1993–96 line-up plays Matador's 21st anniversary weekend in Las Vegas. The tour that follows sells out almost every date, including Maxwell's in Hoboken.

years.h: Let's Go Eat the Factory: first classic-line-up album since 1996
years.p: The reunited band's first album. Class Clown Spots a UFO follows June 12, and The Bears for Lunch in November.

years.h: Kevin Fennell tries to sell the Bee Thousand drum kit
years.p: Drummer Kevin Fennell tries to auction the kit used on Bee Thousand and other albums for $55,000. Robert Pollard says he fired Fennell; Fennell says he quit.

years.h: Cool Planet, with Kevin March on drums
years.p: The sixth reunion album, with Kevin March replacing Kevin Fennell. Motivational Jumpsuit came out in February.

years.h: Guided by Voices breaks up again, by Facebook post
years.p: Guided by Voices abruptly announces it's done on Facebook and cancels the remaining tour dates.

eras.title: A hundred albums and counting
eras.text: Pollard brought the name back with a new band built around Doug Gillard and Kevin March, and has released albums at a rate no one else in rock tries. He stopped touring in 2025.

years.h: Guided by Voices returns to headline Sled Island
years.p: The band announces a June 25 headline slot at Calgary's Sled Island and a new album, Please Be Honest, on which Robert Pollard plays every instrument. Bobby Bare Jr. and Mark Shue join.

years.cap: Doug Gillard back in the band
years.h: Nick Mitchell is fired in the Grog Shop dressing room
years.p: After a set at the Grog Shop in Cleveland, guitarist Nick Mitchell is fired on the spot. Doug Gillard replaces him and rejoins for good later that month.

years.h: August by Cake: Robert Pollard's 100th album
years.p: A double album, and by the count Wikipedia cites, Pollard's 100th release across his bands and solo work. How Do You Spell Heaven follows in August.

years.h: Album 44, and no tour: Pollard says he's too old
years.p: Guided by Voices releases its 44th album, Thick Rich and Delicious. Robert Pollard says the band won't tour it because he feels too old to get onstage.

years.h: Album 45, Crawlspace of the Pantheon, is announced
years.p: Guided by Voices announces Crawlspace of the Pantheon for May 29, 2026, led by the single We Outlast Them All.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Under the Bushes Under the Stars
